description.de: Softwareentwicklung, Betrieb und Vertrieb: Komponenten, Schnittstellen, Releases, Tests, Kampagnen und Verkaufschancen.
description.en: Software development, operations and sales: components, interfaces, releases, tests, campaigns and opportunities.

relations.sentence: Component is part of Software area — the component belongs to this area; a source file belongs to its component, a CI job to its workflow, a tier to the product, a function to the company, a process to its value stream.
Persona belongs to Segment — this persona works at this kind of customer; a role belongs to a function.
Component calls Component — the first invokes the second; read backwards it is called-by.
Component calls back Component — it calls a component that also calls it; read like calls.
Component exposes Interface — the component serves this route.
Interaction is initiated by Component — the calling side.
Interaction is received by Component — the called side.
Commit implements Feature plan — this change is part of carrying out the plan.
Alloy check verifies Invariant — this check proves the invariant holds; a test run verifies a plan or component.
Component contract satisfies Invariant — this clause is how the component upholds the invariant.
Component contract governs Component — this clause applies to this component.
Commit changes Component — the change touched files of this component.

relations.not_to_confuse: imports says a file uses another file's code; defines says where the code lives.
relations.sentence: Source file defines Symbol — the class or function lives in this file. Read backwards: defined in.
Hypothesis is evidenced by Evidence record — this evidence speaks for the claim.
Component keeps Invariant — this component must uphold this invariant.

relations.not_to_confuse: imports links two files; depends_on links components, plans and phases.
relations.sentence: Component depends on Component — it cannot work without the other; a component depends on the libraries its code needs. Read backwards: required by.

relations.not_to_confuse: depends_on links components; imports links two files.
relations.sentence: Source file imports Source file — the first uses code from the second. Read backwards: imported by.

relations.example: Two modules that import each other, one of them inside a function.
relations.not_to_confuse: imports is the first direction of the pair; imports_back exists only because the brain stores one edge per pair and relation.
relations.sentence: Source file imports back Source file — it imports a file that also imports it; read like imports.

relations.not_to_confuse: deployed_in says where the workload runs; executes says what code it runs.
relations.sentence: Service executes Component — the deployed workload runs this component's code. Read backwards: executed by.

relations.not_to_confuse: A deployment records one rollout on a date; deployed_in says where the workload runs today.
relations.sentence: Service is deployed in Environment — the workload or data store runs in this cluster or host. Read backwards: hosts.

relations.not_to_confuse: A release is the versioned whole; builds names the pipeline that produces one image.
relations.sentence: Workflow builds Service — the CI pipeline or job produces the workload's image. Read backwards: built by.

relations.not_to_confuse: writes_to says which component changes the data; stores says where it lives.
relations.sentence: Data store stores Data set — the table or collection lives in this database. Read backwards: stored in.

relations.not_to_confuse: writes_to is the changing side; a component that does both has both edges.
relations.sentence: Component reads from Data set — the component's code reads this table or collection. Read backwards: read by.

relations.not_to_confuse: reads_from is the reading side; stores is where the data lives.
relations.sentence: Component writes to Data set — the component's code inserts, updates or deletes rows of this table or collection. Read backwards: written by.

relations.not_to_confuse: switches is only for feature flags that turn a route or component on or off.
relations.sentence: Component is configured by Setting — the component's code (or the workload's manifest) reads this setting. Read backwards: configures.

relations.example: SET-KG_DOCUMENT_SORTING_ENABLED switches the post-ingest document sorter.
relations.not_to_confuse: configured_by says the code reads the setting; switches says the setting decides whether it runs at all.
relations.sentence: Setting switches Component — this feature flag turns the component or route on or off. Read backwards: switched by.
Hypothesis targets Persona — the claim is about this persona or segment; a campaign targets a segment.
Campaign uses Marketing asset — the campaign sends this one-pager, deck or mail.
Campaign via Channel — the campaign runs through this channel.
Campaign produced Lead — this reply came out of the campaign.
Lead converts to Account — the sales branch moves forward one stage.
Segment is in market Market — this customer type belongs to this market.

description.en: One of the nine large areas the Knovas software is divided into; each has its own responsibility and vocabulary and contains several components (L2).

types.example: L1-RETRIEVE, everything about search and retrieval.
types.not_to_confuse: A capability describes what a customer can do, not how the software is split.

description.en: The Knovas software as a whole; its software areas are part of it, and its reference documentation starts here.

types.example: SYS-KNOVAS-SEMANTIX, the Knovas Semantix platform.
types.not_to_confuse: A product is what Knovas sells; the system is the software that runs it.

description.en: The route path, e.g. /secured/query.
The HTTP methods the route accepts.
The code file that registers the route.
The contract page that describes the route.
Whether the route is operational (health, metrics) rather than a product function.

no.text: A route that offers a product function.

yes.text: An operational route such as /health or /metrics.

description.en: An HTTP route a software component serves, with its methods and the page that documents it; read from the code.

types.example: IF-secure_api:/secured/query, the search route of the Secure API.
types.not_to_confuse: A capability is what a customer can do; an interface is one technical entry point.

description.en: What the calling component invokes on the other.
How the call travels: in-process, HTTP, a queue, …
What the call guarantees, as the interaction catalogue describes it.
Which documents declare the interaction.
One software component calling another: which methods, over which protocol, under which contract.

types.example: IX-L2-SECURE-API--L2-QUERY-2STAGE, the Secure API passing a search to the two-stage query engine.
types.not_to_confuse: An interface is the entry point; an interaction is who calls whom through it.

description.en: Where the component's calls to other components are declared, or that no source declares any.
The design pattern the component follows, from its spec (e.g. Facade with Decorator).
Whether the component's formal models cover it, as the manifest says.
Whether a component folder with README and spec exists.
Where the component's code lives, from the manifest.
The component's human name from the manifest.
A part of the Knovas software with a clear responsibility, its own documentation and tests, inside one software area.

types.example: L2-KNOWLEDGE-GRAPH, the knowledge graph the brain is built on.
types.not_to_confuse: A source file is a single code file; a component is the unit engineers own and document.

description.en: Precondition, postcondition or responsibility.

precondition.text: Must hold before the component runs.

responsibility.text: What the component is responsible for.

description.en: A promise a component makes: what must be true before it runs (precondition), what is true afterwards (postcondition), or what it is responsible for.

types.example: L2-KNOWLEDGE-GRAPH/POST-P0-01, new chunks carry the access scope of their document from the moment they exist.
types.not_to_confuse: An invariant holds for the whole system; a contract belongs to one component.

description.en: Coverage as the catalog page states it (pytest, Alloy, planned).
The area of the system the invariant belongs to.
A rule the whole system must keep at all times, written down with an id, verified by tests and formal checks.

types.example: GI-GRAPH-13, document sorting only ever proposes; the client decides.
types.not_to_confuse: A component contract is local to one part; an invariant is system-wide.

description.en: A region and offering Knovas sells into.

types.example: MKT-01, DACH, the True Graph company brain.

description.en: Where the segment is served.
A kind of customer Knovas targets, the ideal customer profile.

types.example: ICP-03, law firms in Switzerland and Germany.
types.not_to_confuse: A persona is a person inside such a customer; a segment is the company type.

description.en: Champion, economic buyer, user, …
Version and date of the persona sheet.
An archetype of a person in the buying centre of a customer, with pains, goals and a role in the deal.

types.example: P-10, the senior lawyer who is the practice group's memory.

description.en: How a segment is reached: direct, resellers, software vendors, events, content.

types.example: CH-RESELLERS.

description.en: Where the instance stands in its process; written by the loader and dated with the day the instance entered the step (DEC-0018).
Every step the instance went through with its start and end day, kept by the loader; the flow view measures lead times from it.
Planned, running, done, or exploration when the thresholds were not set before the start.

exploration.text: Thresholds not set before the start: counts, not evidence.

description.en: The metric the keep and kill thresholds are set on (reply rate, meeting rate, …).
How many sent before a result counts.
The rate at which we keep the approach.
The rate at which we stop it.
The A/B variants, if any, as a list.
First day of the campaign.
Planned end date; the evaluation runs after it.

A marketing effort aimed at a segment and its personas, run as a registered experiment: it tests a persona hypothesis with a metric, a minimum sample and keep and kill thresholds set before it starts.

types.example: CMP-2026-11-icp01-head-of-dev, a call campaign to 40 ICP-01 heads of development.
types.not_to_confuse: An experiment is the general type; a campaign is the marketing kind of it and appears on the same board.

description.en: A one-pager, deck, demo or case study written for a persona.

types.example: The reseller intro deck.

description.en: Where the instance stands in its process; written by the loader and dated with the day the instance entered the step (DEC-0018).
Every step the instance went through with its start and end day, kept by the loader; the flow view measures lead times from it.
The segment the lead belongs to.
The account (company) the lead belongs to.
The persona the contact's role maps to.
Economic buyer, champion, user, … (never a name).
New, replied, meeting, opportunity or dropped.
A company that showed interest in a campaign, stored as the account plus the buying-centre role mapped to a persona, never as a name or contact detail (privacy rule).

types.example: LEAD-cmp-2026-11-icp01-acc-0007, economic buyer (P-03) at account ACC-0007.
types.not_to_confuse: An opportunity is a qualified deal with a stage; a lead is the first reply.

description.en: Where the instance stands in its process; written by the loader and dated with the day the instance entered the step (DEC-0018).
Every step the instance went through with its start and end day, kept by the loader; the flow view measures lead times from it.
Where the deal stands in the pipeline.

qualified.text: Worth pursuing (economic buyer and pain known).

description.en: Do we know how the customer measures success?
Do we know who holds the budget and signs?
Do we know the must-haves and nice-to-haves?
Do we know who recommends, decides and confirms?
Do we know the contracts and approvals needed?
Do we know what it costs the customer to do nothing?
Do we have an internal advocate?
Do we know what else the customer considers?
One note per element.
The company the deal is with.
The deal value, as text with currency and period.
What happens next in the deal.
When the next step is due.
The roles in the deal mapped to personas, never names.
A deal in the sales pipeline with its stage and its MEDDPICC qualification.

types.example: A proof of concept with a Treuhand firm, stage quote.

description.en: The quoted amount.
A priced offer: articles, seats, API buckets.

types.example: 20 Cortex seats for a law firm.

description.en: A git repository holding code or documents.

types.example: KnowledgeBase.

description.en: A fingerprint of the file, to notice changes.
The name other code uses to import the file, e.g. services.query_pipeline.
The file's size in bytes.
When the file last changed in the repository.
One code or model file in a repository, with a content hash so changes are noticed.

types.example: knovas-software/app/src/api/graph_api.py.

description.en: Module, class, function or method.
Where it starts in the file.
A class, function or method inside a source file.

types.example: graph_api.py#create_node.

description.en: The commit date.
Who made the commit.
The first line of the commit message.
The pull request the commit merged, if any.
One recorded change to a repository, linked to the plan it implements and the components it touched.

types.example: COMMIT-215b05af5f77, the merge of Client Zero Phase 0.

description.en: Passed, failed or skipped.
When the tests ran.
How many tests the module has.
How many failed.
The result of running one test module on a date: passed or failed, how many tests.

types.example: tests/test_document_sorter.py on 25 Oct 2026, passed.

description.en: Where the instance stands in its process; written by the loader and dated with the day the instance entered the step (DEC-0018).
Every step the instance went through with its start and end day, kept by the loader; the flow view measures lead times from it.
The version label of the release.
Dev or prod.
The date it reached the environment.
Candidate, verified, deployed or announced.

A versioned release of the software moving from candidate through verified and deployed to announced; recorded by the engine owner in releases.yaml because no git tag or deploy flow marks releases today.

types.example: REL-2026.10-brain-mvp, the brain MVP on cloudscale prod, 24 Oct 2026.
types.not_to_confuse: A deployment is one rollout to one environment; a release is the versioned whole that may be deployed to dev and then prod.

description.en: Dev or prod.
The deployment date.
A release of the software to an environment on a date.

types.example: The brain MVP on cloudscale prod, 24 Oct 2026.

description.en: The container image the service runs, without its version tag.
Whether the service is reachable only inside the cluster or from outside.

public.text: Reachable from outside through a gateway, ingress or load balancer.

description.en: A piece of the software that is deployed and keeps running, such as an API server or the embedding service; it executes one or more components in one or more environments.

types.example: SVC-secure-api, the mTLS API for clients, running on cloudscale prod and AKS dev.
types.not_to_confuse: A component is a part of the code that engineers own; a service is what is deployed and running. A deployment is one rollout on a date. A product service (euo:Service) is something sold.

description.en: When the job starts, as a cron expression.
The container image the job runs, without its version tag.
A piece of the software that is started on a schedule, does its work and stops, such as a nightly aggregation.

types.example: JOB-analytics-aggregation, the nightly analytics roll-up on cloudscale prod.
types.not_to_confuse: A CI job (workflow job) builds and tests code; a scheduled job runs in an environment. An agent is the actor a run is recorded against.

description.en: Local, dev or prod.

prod.text: A production cluster with customer data or traffic.

description.en: Where the cluster or host runs: AKS, cloudscale, AWS, Lambda Labs, Docker Compose.
A place where the software runs: one cluster or host of one stage, local, dev or prod.

types.example: ENV-knovas-cloudscale-prod, the production cluster at cloudscale that holds the customer data.
types.not_to_confuse: A stage (dev, prod) is a property of an environment; prod has more than one environment (AKS and cloudscale).

description.en: Relational, key-value, vector, object store or other.
The product and how it is run, e.g. PostgreSQL with CloudNativePG.
A database, cache, vector index or file store the software keeps data in; it holds tables or collections.

types.example: DS-postgres, the PostgreSQL cluster with clients, certificates and the usage ledger.
types.not_to_confuse: A data set is one table or collection inside it; the data store is the database as a whole.

description.en: Table, collection, bucket, keyspace or other.

bucket.text: A container of a file or blob store.

collection.text: A collection of a vector or document database.

keyspace.text: A group of keys in a key-value store.

description.en: The table's columns with their types, as the migrations leave them.
One table, collection, bucket or keyspace inside a data store, with the components that read and write it.

types.example: DATA-weaviate/SentenceChunk, the stored text chunks with their embeddings.
types.not_to_confuse: A data store is the database; a data set is one table in it. A record is a document, not data.

description.en: A plain setting, a feature flag or a secret.

feature-flag.text: A switch that turns a function on or off.

secret.text: A password, key or token; its value is never recorded.

setting.text: A value that tunes how the software behaves.

description.en: The value the software uses when no environment overrides it; empty for a secret.
The part of the defaults file the key is in; empty for the top.
Whether the default is a yes/no switch, a number, a text or a list.
One configuration key the software reads, with its default: a plain setting, a feature flag that switches something on or off, or a secret whose value is never recorded.

types.example: SET-KG_DOCUMENT_SORTING_ENABLED, the feature flag for identifier-based document sorting, off by default.
types.not_to_confuse: The value in one environment is a property of that environment's configuration; the setting is the key and its default.

description.en: The events that start the workflow, such as a push, a pull request or a schedule.
The files and folders whose change starts the workflow or one of its jobs.
An automated pipeline that tests, checks, builds or deploys the software when something happens, such as a push or a schedule; made of jobs.

types.example: WF-ci, the main pipeline: tests, Alloy checks, image builds and deploy.
types.not_to_confuse: A process is how people's work moves; a workflow is a machine pipeline. A test run is one result, not the pipeline.

description.en: The jobs of the same workflow that must finish first.
One job of a CI workflow, such as running the tests or building the images; it may wait for other jobs.

types.example: WF-ci/alloy-checks, the bounded Alloy checks in the main pipeline.
types.not_to_confuse: A scheduled job runs in an environment; a CI job runs in the pipeline.

description.en: Where the package comes from: PyPI, npm, Maven or other.
The version the code pins or requires.
The package's licence as an SPDX id.
A third-party package the software uses, with its version and licence.

types.example: LIB-pypi:flask, the web framework of the two Flask APIs.
types.not_to_confuse: A component is Knovas's own code; a library is someone else's.
